rationaleAppend: Cross-reference (isaiah-woh wave I-5, founder sign-off 2026-11-26): at Isa 31:8 the bare noun mas (ûḇaḥûrāyw lāmas yihyû) is rendered 'his young men shall become forced labor' (isaiah-woh overlay lexical-cruxes-isaiah-31). 'Forced labor' is the standard modern lexical sense of collective mas (BDB 'body of forced labourers'; HALOT 'forced labour, corvée'; recalled, not verified), where ASV has 'subject to taskwork', JPS 1917 'tributary' and NJPS, deriving the word from mss, 'pine away'. This entry keeps ASV 'taskwork' for the compound mas ʿōḇēḏ at Gen 49:15 and its wohChoice is unchanged. The corpus therefore has two English words for mas: 'taskwork' in the compound and 'forced labor' for mas alone. A corpus-wide decision on bare mas is recommended before Kings (1 Kgs 5:27; 9:15, 21) reaches the library.
